I farm 6 mu here in Quzhou, same wheat-maize rotation I've been doing most of my life. I'm alone in the house now, so labor is tight — whatever I plan, I have to do myself or pay someone, and paying costs money.

I'll start with last year's plan and adjust a little. For wheat I always use improved seed — I buy from the dealer in town, about 15 kg per mu, drill-sown after maize comes off in October. Before sowing I spread compound fertilizer as base — I use about 50 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu, that gives me roughly 7.5 kg each of N, P, K from the base. Then at jointing in spring I topdress urea, about 20 kg per mu (that's about 9 kg N). So total for wheat: around 16-17 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K per mu. I'd rather put on a bit extra than watch the crop turn yellow — a bad wheat harvest is real loss, fertilizer is just money spent.

Wheat needs water. I irrigate at sowing (tamping water), then winter water before freeze, jointing in spring, and grain-filling — that's 4 times from the well. Pesticide: one herbicide spray in late winter/early spring for grass weeds, and one mix at heading for aphids and powdery mildew. Two applications. I plough-rotary before sowing wheat since I want a clean seedbed after maize stalks.

For summer maize after wheat harvest in June — hybrid seed, everyone around uses Zhengdan or Xianyu type hybrids, they yield well. I direct-seed no-till into the wheat stubble with the planter, saves time since I'm alone. Base fertilizer at sowing, compound 15-15-15 about 40 kg per mu, then big topdress of urea at big-trumpet stage (V12), about 25 kg per mu. Total maize: about 17-18 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. Irrigate once after sowing if no rain, and once at tasseling if dry — usually 2 times. Spray: one for corn borer, sometimes one for armyworm if I see them. Two applications.

Yields — my wheat runs around 480 kg/mu in a normal year, maize about 600 kg/mu. I'll plan for that.
